solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: River Test suitable for factories?

parts.note: the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: An angler wonders whether the River Test, a Hampshire trout stream, could be turned over to industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Test is a famous English chalk stream, but here 'River' and 'Test' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit for factories belongs to manufacturing, the adjective for heavy production.

clue.text: They don't appear to eat or wash regularly

parts.note: nosh is slang meaning to eat

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: People who neglect meals and baths, so are never seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees who miss an event they were booked for are the people who fail to turn up.

clue.text: Complete idiot needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the first letter of the slang word goes

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A total fool so famous that nobody needs to present him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like it describes the idiot, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and complete both mean total, absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Boat going off? I dumped sledge

indicators.note: off says the letters of the first two words are rearranged
dumped says the letter from the following word is thrown out of the pool

explanation.surface: A boat heading out, so the speaker jumped ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles BOAT GOING once 'I dumped' takes out its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, flat sled for sliding downhill on snow.

clue.text: Fiery Toscanini hosts irate queen by lake, fiddling

indicators.note: hosts means one piece takes the other inside it
fiery says the conductor's name is in a passion, its letters thrown about
irate says the word queen is in a rage, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: The famously temperamental conductor Toscanini entertains an angry queen beside a lake, playing violin.
explanation.walkthrough: Toscanini was a notoriously fiery Italian conductor, so 'Fiery' reads as a description, not a signal. 'fiddling' suggests violin playing but means trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddling in the sense of petty or trifling means unimportant.

clue.text: Two birds regurgitated seeds

definitions.note: a plural for a singular: the pod is a seed vessel holding peas or beans

indicators.note: regurgitated means the two birds come back up in reverse order

parts.note: an emu is a flightless bird, and gel is a posh pronunciation of girl, slang bird

explanation.surface: Two birds bring back up the seeds they swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is slang for a young woman, and a gel is a girl in a cut-glass accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils, the edible seeds of pod plants, are this food group.

clue.text: Did 13, as stated, box?

indicators.note: as stated means the past-tense word is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: 13 across is OSCULATE, so 'did 13' is a past-tense smooch

explanation.surface: A cross-reference riddle asking whether a past act could be a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 13 means to plant a smacker; its past tense, said out loud, is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kist is a Scottish and northern English word for a chest or coffer.

clue.text: Position textbook?

parts.note: a textbook of positions, read as sexual positions

explanation.surface: Asking for a manual on stances or postures.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Sanskrit text is famous as a guide to lovemaking postures.

clue.text: Game sister tackles it after I quit

indicators.note: tackles means the sister abbreviation takes on, and so holds, the other piece
quit says the letter I leaves the slang word

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex, as is nookie

explanation.surface: A sister takes on a game after the speaker gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' means sex here, a common crossword euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: The cue sport played with fifteen reds and six colours.

clue.text: Noisy drunk that attracts attention

indicators.note: noisy says the slang word for drunk is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A loud drunk is the sort who gets everyone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for inebriated; said quickly it sounds like the whispered call.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered interjection is used to catch someone's notice discreetly.

clue.text: Two slices of pork or game

parts.note: back bacon and gammon are two cuts of cured pork
gammon is the second of the two cured pork cuts

explanation.surface: A butcher's choice between two cuts of pork or some game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like venison or pheasant beside the pork, but it is the definition. Back and gammon are both British cuts of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Despicable guy brought back, given time inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for time is placed within the other piece
back means the word for brought is read in the other direction

parts.note: got can mean brought, as in got the shopping in
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lowlife returned to custody and handed a jail sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given time' suggests a prison sentence; time here is an age or epoch instead. TOERAG is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a contemptible, worthless man.

clue.text: Seek a man out who's confused with someone else

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the first three words are to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Go looking for a man who keeps being mistaken for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'out' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sharing someone's name is liable to be mixed up with them.

clue.text: Pay lip service to very big copper behind schedule?

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Paying empty respect to a huge police officer who is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss is literally to serve with the lips, a witty twist on the idiom for insincere support.

clue.text: Guide turned out to be lacking instruction

indicators.note: guide, steer the letters of the next two words into a new order

explanation.surface: A guide proved to have had no training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' looks like the subject but is the anagram signal; 'turned' is fodder, not an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never taught by a teacher is unschooled.

clue.text: City Remoulds supply it

indicators.note: supply means the first two words provide the letters, sitting across the join between them

explanation.surface: A town where retreaded wheels are on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' tempts as a definition (there is an ancient Lebanese port of that name), but the letters straddle 'City Remoulds', and the whole clue defines: remoulds are retreads.
explanation.definitionFit: A remould is a retreaded wheel cover, so remoulds furnish one.

clue.text: Doctor brought up nurses to encourage new writer

indicators.note: nurses means holds, as in nursing a drink, so one piece cradles the other
brought up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
to urge is to encourage

explanation.surface: A doctor reared by nurses who encourage a new author.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was the Russian novelist of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Leave this way, about to be expelled

indicators.note: to be expelled says the short word for about is thrown out of the road word

parts.note: a street is a way, as in road names
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave this way because they are about to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave this way' reads as directions out, but the definition is 'Leave this', the proofreader's mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The proof-correction instruction, Latin for let it stand, tells the printer to keep the text as it was.

clue.text: Practise wrestling without one? Unlikely

indicators.note: wrestling says the letters of practise grapple into a new order
without says the letter for one is left out of the pool

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Wrestling training without the muscle at the back of the arm is improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling' shuffles PRACTISE once 'without' removes A (one), and the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm is vital for grappling, so training without it is unlikely.

clue.text: Singer, upset with worried daughter, wailed

indicators.note: upset means the singer's name is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer
ate can mean worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A singer, distressed alongside her anxious daughter, cried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like an anagram signal but is ATE, worried in the sense of gnawed at.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to howl or wail, often in grief.

clue.text: He takes flight in case fresh relief needed

indicators.note: fresh says the letters of case are made anew

parts.note: to pee is to relieve oneself

explanation.surface: Someone running off in case a new bout of relief is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' sounds like rescue but is the comfort break.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has fled from captivity has taken flight.

clue.text: Muggy day stopped trading

parts.note: close weather is humid and muggy

explanation.surface: On a humid day a shop shut early.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that has shut its doors for business has ceased to deal.

clue.text: Book one Irish town briefly for contest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: briefly means the town's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the Irish Midlands

explanation.surface: Reserving a single Irish town for a short time to host a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The biathlon is a sporting event combining skiing and shooting.

clue.text: Marx doesn't finish beef

indicators.note: doesn't finish means the last letter of the comedian's name is dropped

parts.note: Groucho Marx was the moustached comedian of the Marx Brothers

explanation.surface: A Marx — Karl, presumably — leaves his complaint unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx suggests Karl, but it is Groucho, the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and grouch are both slang for a complaint or grumble.

clue.text: Proprietor's 25, heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut from the word for a slump

parts.note: 25 across is a slump, and a downer is a state of low spirits

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: the boss is clue 25 minus its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who possesses a business or property.

clue.text: Prof passes round English papers — I slump

indicators.note: passes round means the academic surrounds the following pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, like a professor
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A professor hands out English papers while the speaker sags in their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I slump' reads as a confession; 'I' is a letter and 'slump' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic slump is a prolonged downturn in trade.

clue.text: New primate has some neck!

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A newly arrived monkey shows some cheek, or rather some neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has some neck' sounds like impudence; it points to part of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the neck carries this name.

clue.text: Second-hand American edition

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A pre-owned copy of an American edition of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have been owned before, so previously owned.

clue.text: Consignments food shop confirms, no doubt

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: no says the word for doubt is removed

parts.note: verifies means confirms
if can mean a doubt, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A grocer confirms beyond doubt that the shipments have arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no doubt' reads as certainty; here it means remove IF from VERIFIES, leaving VERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Batches of goods sent out are shipments brought to the door.
